acceptance: Smoke: `make ci-linux CI_LINUX_CMD=true` holds the host lock during the run (a WAIT_SECONDS=0 acquire is refused) and, per G1, leaves the machine in its prior state; output recorded.

description:
## Problem
Two call sites boot the 4 CPU / 8 GiB `benchbox-agent` machine: `make ci-linux` (Makefile:883) and `scripts/linux_preflight_pytest.sh:66` (reached from `make pr-preflight`). The host takes no lock around them, and the machine stays running afterwards (6.06 GiB resident during the incident). Compose bring-ups (`make/platform-tests.mk:80,137,150`; `test-docker-up-all` :172-202 starts 12 stacks; `scripts/uat-bring-up/uat_bring_up.py:131`) start long-lived containers with no admission check.

## Change
1. Wrap both `container machine run` call sites with `python -m benchbox.utils.host_lock run --guard -- ...` on the host. The host watchdog covers pressure and disk only: `container` runtime and VM processes are children of launchd, so VM memory is not tree-attributed; machine size and admission bound it.
2. After the run, stop the machine only if this invocation started it (record state before; leave it running if it already was).
3. Change documented machine size in setup text (Makefile:879 and the `linux_preflight_pytest.sh` setup message) from 8G to 6G.
4. Compose admission only for callers that hold no lock: one Make variable used by every `up` recipe in `make/platform-tests.mk` runs `python -m benchbox.utils.host_lock admit --need-gib <declared>` first; `uat_bring_up.py` does the same with need from `compose_declared_memory_limits`. Callers inside a locked UAT run (`tests/uat/phases/execute.py:326`) are unchanged; `_free_memory_abort_reason` keeps owning that path.
5. Choke-point test in the required fast unit lane (`fast` + `unit`): parse Makefile, `make/*.mk`, `scripts/**/*.sh`, `_project/scripts/**/*.sh`; every `container machine run` and `compose ... up` goes through the wrapper/variable (echo/usage lines excluded); Python `compose ... up` argv is built only by `compose_up_command`.
6. `make/help.mk` lines for any new public target.

## Decision gates
- D1 (resolved): the pr-preflight Linux step waits on the lock like any heavy run; update `docs/agent/dev-loop-worktrees.md:240-244` to name this exception.
- G1 (stop condition): verify whether `container machine run` auto-starts a stopped machine. If not, do not stop it after runs; record the finding.
- G2 (operator gate): resizing the existing machine is an operator action; do it only when no `container machine run` is active and no other session uses it; otherwise record a deferral with the exact command.
- G3 (coordination): open item `uat-docker-memory-admission-decimal-units-20261030` edits `tests/uat/docker_assets.py`; if this item must touch that file, rebase after it lands.

## Guardrails (all heavy-guard items)
- Linked worktree from `origin/develop` via `make worktree-create`; never the primary clone; stage paths explicitly; never `git add -A`.
- `[COMMENT-POLICY-001]`: no comments or docstrings in new code. Durations use `benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time()`/`elapsed_seconds()`.
- Tests use `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR` under `tmp_path` and injected readings; never touch the real `~/.benchbox/test.lock` or depend on live host pressure, VMs or disk.
- Never delete, move or recreate a lock file from code; never stop, resize or signal processes/VMs this invocation did not start.
- Keep names `test.lock`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS`, `BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_SESSION_OWNER` (rename deferred on heavy-guard-status-policy).
- No automatic skip on `CI` or `BENCHBOX_EPHEMERAL_CLONE` (agent shells export `CI=true`).
- No heavy verification runs (no benchmark sweeps above scale 0.01, no real compose stacks) unless the item names one.
- `docs/internal/makefile-architecture.md:34`: do not regenerate `make/monolith-baseline.json` or `make/migration-proof.json`.

## Non-goals
Lease processes for compose stacks (rejected: deadlocks `make test-docker-up-X && uat sweep`; wrong engine on this host).
